text: Welcome to the season finale of the Apex
Energy Summer Series presented by Boone
Chrysler Dodge Jeep and Ram. And this
week we'll be heading to the Homestead
Miami Speedway for 117 laps as we cap
off the week. Let's hop straight into
qualifying one more time.
As always, you'll want to spend your
first laps building heat in your tires.
As you make your way around the track to
prepare for your hot lap, try running
around the seam on the outside.
If you can keep the car turning at a
steady radius using that seam as a
reference, you'll be able to put down a
solid lap once you take the white flag.
Get as much momentum as you can as you
cross the line to begin your final lap.
Heading into turn one, take a wide
entry, trail brake, and get the car
guided as close to the white line as you
can.
Once you feel the car rotate on the
inside, get back on the gas and hold on
for dear life as you exit turn two.
Round off your exit, try not to get too
close to the outside wall until you get
closer to turns three and four.
Once you reach the entry, lift off the
gas, trail brake down at the bottom, and
let the car roll slightly longer before
you get back on the gas. There are a few
bumps on that end of the track, so it'll
be easy to wash up and catch the wall if
you aren't careful.
Round off your exit once again and take
the checkered flag.
If you were able to carry as much speed
as possible using the shortest distance
around the corner, you'll find yourself
in a great position for the start.
Once the race begins, you know the
drill.
Hang out around the inside and conserve
your tires for the late stages of the
green flag run.
As the bottom line heats up, you may be
able to find some extra speed further up
the track, but I would advise against it
unless you're confident that you have a
tire advantage. They could burn up
quickly up there, so be careful.
With that being said, the outside will
be the place to be if you want to
maintain your track position. If you
want to see what that might look like
toward the end of the race, take a look
at the last 20 laps of last week's
Atlanta broadcast.
By the end, there will still be speed to
find on the inside, but if you have a
line of cars sitting in the outside
lane, you'll be dead in the water. So,
keep that in mind when you find your
position late in the race.
If you can keep your tires under you and
make the right moves as the laps wind
down, you might find yourself near the
front when it's all said and done.
After hosting 147 drivers and 28
different winners across over 100 races,
all good things must come to an end. So,
let's send the Slingshot Racing League
off with one more show.
Good luck.
